fact: The Nzika Digital ID Wallet, which lets citizens securely present verified identity credentials digitally, was officially launched in Lilongwe, the article says.
The Homeland Security Minister said citizens can adopt a digital credential through the Nzika Digital ID Wallet as an option alongside the physical card.
The Homeland Security Minister said verification will now rely on real-time biometrics against the National Registration Bureau database.
The Nzika Wallet lets citizens present verified credentials digitally and can be used to access services before receiving a physical card, per the Homeland Security Minister.
The Nzika Digital ID Wallet launched in Lilongwe on 2026-09-16, letting citizens store and present government-issued credentials on a phone, per Malawi24.
Malawi24 reports the official wallet holds credentials including the Citizen Identification and presents them by QR code from a mobile phone.
UNDP says Malawi launched the Nzika Digital ID Wallet on 2026-09-16 and became the fifth African country to operationalise an ID wallet.
UNDP says the wallet gives citizens a platform to access and manage official credentials including National IDs, birth, marriage and death certificates.

The Nzika Digital ID Wallet was launched in Lilongwe on 16 September 2026 by the National Registration Bureau with partners including UNDP, with more than 22,000 reportedly enrolled by launch, per the Maravi Post column.

Nzika is a digital identity wallet that lets citizens hold digital versions of their National ID and certain civil registration documents, which the column says could make it easier to prove who they are.
The column says World Bank-supported programmes include plans involving digital identity authentication, electronic signatures and electronic know-your-customer services.
